arxiv-1909-04654.title: The prospect of charm quark magnetic moment determination
arxiv-1909-04654.creator: A.S. Fomin, S. Barsuk, A.Yu. Korchin, V.A. Kovalchuk, E. Kou, M. Liul, A. Natochii, E. Niel, P. Robbe, A. Stocchi
arxiv-1909-04654.description: Abstract In this paper, we discuss the theoretical framework and the experimental measurements of the magnetic moment of the charm baryons. The Λ c + \Lambda_{c}^{+} magnetic moment is particularly interesting since it is equal to the magnetic moment of the charm quark.

arxiv-2107-10630.title: Are GRMHD Mean-Field Dynamo Models of Thick Accretion Disks SANE?
arxiv-2107-10630.creator: Niccolò Tomei *, Luca Del Zanna, Matteo Bugli, Niccolò Bucciantini
arxiv-2107-10630.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Niccolò Tomei *, Luca Del Zanna, Matteo Bugli, Niccolò Bucciantini. The remarkable results by the Event Horizon Telescope collaboration concerning the emission from M87* and, more recently, its polarization properties, require an increasingly accurate modeling of the plasma flows around the accreting black hole.

arxiv-2205-02157.title: Arrangement for K 2 ∗ K_{2}^{*} meson family
arxiv-2205-02157.creator: Ting-Yan Li 1,2, Ya-rong Wang 1,2, Cheng-qun Pang 1,2,3
arxiv-2205-02157.description: Abstract Two observed structures with M = 1868 ± 8 − 57 + 40 M=1868\pm 8^{+40}_{-57} MeV and M = 2073 ± 94 − 240 + 245 M=2073\pm 94^{+245}_{-240} MeV are the same states ( K 2 ∗ ​ ( 1980 ) K_{2}^{*}(1980) ) in PDG.

arxiv-2208-11750.title: Magnetic cooling and vibration isolation of a sub-kHz mechanical resonator
arxiv-2208-11750.creator: Bernard van Heck, Tim M. Fuchs, Jaimy Plugge, Wim A. Bosch, Tjerk H. Oosterkamp
arxiv-2208-11750.description: Abstract We report recent progress towards the realization of a sub-mK, low-vibration environment at the bottom stage of a dry dilution refrigerator for use in mechanical tests of quantum mechanics. Using adiabatic nuclear demagnetization, we have cooled a silicon cantilever force sensor to T ≈ 1 T\approx 1 mK.

arxiv-2312-08110.title: Tailored and Externally Corrected Coupled Cluster with Quantum Inputs
arxiv-2312-08110.creator: Maximilian Scheurer, Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Oumarou Oumarou, Christian Gogolin, Nicholas C. Rubin
arxiv-2312-08110.description: Abstract We propose to use wavefunction overlaps obtained from a quantum computer as inputs for the classical split-amplitude techniques, tailored and externally corrected coupled cluster, to achieve balanced treatment of static and dynamic correlation effects in molecular electronic structure simulations.

arxiv-2403-09736.title: Negative pressure in the quantum vacuum
arxiv-2403-09736.creator: Zhentao Zhang
arxiv-2403-09736.description: Abstract It is well known that a constant energy density of the vacuum produces a negative pressure. We show that, in the presence of special boundaries for the photon field, the virtual photons in the quantum vacuum may induce a negative pressure of this type.

arxiv-2407-05996.title: Multimodal Diffusion Transformer: Learning Versatile Behavior from Multimodal Goals
arxiv-2407-05996.creator: Moritz Reuss, Ömer Erdinç Yağmurlu, Fabian Wenzel, Rudolf Lioutikov
arxiv-2407-05996.description: Abstract This work introduces the Multimodal Diffusion Transformer (MDT), a novel diffusion policy framework, that excels at learning versatile behavior from multimodal goal specifications with few language annotations. MDT leverages a diffusion-based multimodal transformer backbone and two self-supervised auxiliary objectives to master long-horizon manipulation tasks based on multimodal goals.

arxiv-2505-21005.title: Efficient and Unbiased Sampling from Boltzmann Distributions via Variance-Tuned Diffusion Models
arxiv-2505-21005.creator: Fengzhe Zhang, Laurence I. Midgley, José Miguel Hernández-Lobato
arxiv-2505-21005.description: Abstract Score-based diffusion models (SBDMs) are powerful amortized samplers for Boltzmann distributions; however, imperfect score estimates bias downstream Monte Carlo estimates. Classical importance sampling (IS) can correct this bias, but computing exact likelihoods requires solving the probability-flow ordinary differential equation (PF–ODE), a procedure that is prohibitively costly and scales poorly with dimensionality.

arxiv-2511-03187.title: Periodic Skill Discovery
arxiv-2511-03187.creator: Jonghae Park Daesol Cho Jusuk Lee Dongseok Shim Inkyu Jang H. Jin Kim
arxiv-2511-03187.description: Abstract Unsupervised skill discovery in reinforcement learning (RL) aims to learn diverse behaviors without relying on external rewards. However, current methods often overlook the periodic nature of learned skills, focusing instead on increasing the mutual dependence between states and skills or maximizing the distance traveled in latent space.

pmc-10483867.title: “Dual sensitive supramolecular curcumin nanoparticles” in “advanced yeast particles” mediate macrophage reprogramming, ROS scavenging and inflammation resolution for ulcerative colitis treatment
pmc-10483867.creator: Xiaoqin Han, Ruifeng Luo, Shanshan Qi, Yanli Wang, Linxin Dai, Wenbiao Nie, Meisi Lin, Haoqi He, Naijing Ye, Chaomei Fu, Yu You, Shu Fu, Fei Gao
pmc-10483867.description: Ulcerative colitis (UC) faces some barriers in oral therapy, such as how to safely deliver drugs to the colon and accumulate in the colon lesions. Hence, we report an advanced yeast particles system loaded with supramolecular nanoparticles with ROS scavenger (curcumin) to treat UC by reducing oxidative stress state and inflammatory response and accelerating the reprogramming of macrophages.

pmc-10743866.title: Clinical Outcomes of Next-Generation Microwave Thermosphere Ablation for Hepatocellular Carcinoma with Primarily Hepatitis-Related Etiology
pmc-10743866.creator: Shinichiro Nakamura, Toshifumi Tada, Masahiko Sue, Yu Matsuo, Shiho Murakami, Toshiro Muramatsu, Kazuhiko Morii, Hiroyuki Okada, David E Kaplan
pmc-10743866.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background and aim: We investigated the clinical outcomes of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) who underwent next-generation microwave thermosphere ablation (MTA). Methods: A total of 429 patients with 607 HCCs (maximum tumor diameter ≤40 mm) were included.

pmc-11421448.title: Impact of Altered Gut Microbiota on Ketamine-Induced Conditioned Place Preference in Mice
pmc-11421448.creator: Chan Li, Chen Zhu, Genghong Tu, Zhijie Chen, Zhixian Mo, Chaohua Luo
pmc-11421448.description: ObjectsKetamine is a drug of abuse worldwide and current treatments for ketamine abuse are inadequate. It is an urgent need to develop novel anti-addictive strategy. Since gut microbiota plays a crucial role in drug abuse, the present study investigates the impact and mechanisms of the gut microbiota in addictive behaviors induced by ketamine addiction.

pmc-11435944.title: Structural Plastic Damage Warning and Real-Time Sensing System Based on Cointegration Theory
pmc-11435944.creator: Qiang Gao, Junzhou Huo, Youfu Wang, Xiaotian Wang, Chongru Wang
pmc-11435944.description: Structural damage can affect the long-term operation of equipment. Real-time damage warning for structures can effectively avoid accidents caused by structural damage. In this paper, a real-time warning method of structural plastic damage based on the cointegration theory is proposed.

pmc-11654275.title: A qualitative study exploring stakeholders’ perceptions of registry-based randomised controlled trials capacity and capability in Australia
pmc-11654275.creator: Bill Karanatsios, Khic-Houy Prang, Justin M Yeung, Peter Gibbs
pmc-11654275.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundTraditional randomised controlled trials (RCTs) are the gold standard for evaluating the effectiveness of interventions in clinical research. Traditional RCTs however are complex, expensive and have low external validity. Registry-based randomised controlled trials (RRCTs) are an emerging alternative approach that integrates the internal validity of a traditional RCT with the external validity of a clinical registry by recruiting more real-world patients and leveraging an existing registry platform for data collection.

pmc-11689307.title: COMPUTER-MEDIATED COMMUNICATION (CMC) AND SOCIAL ENGAGEMENT AMONG INDIVIDUALS WITH ALZHEIMER’S
pmc-11689307.creator: Yun Leng Wong, Laura Hemmy, Mike Conway, Daniel Cabrera Lozoya, Kelvin Lim, Jude Mikal
pmc-11689307.description: Normal aging confers a host of risk factors for loneliness and social isolation. Aging accompanied by Alzheimer’s-related changes in cognition and function may result in even higher risk of loneliness and social isolation. Nevertheless, older adults now represent the fastest-growing demographic of both Internet and social media users.

pmc-12436436.title: Exploring neurodevelopment through oscillatory and aperiodic EEG activity: methodological and clinical consideration
pmc-12436436.creator: Stefania Petri, Helene Vitali, Claudio Campus, Martina Riberto, Monica Gori
pmc-12436436.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Understanding the neural dynamics that characterize early brain development is a central goal in neuroscience. Electroencephalography (EEG), is particularly well suited for studying the developing brain, given to its non-invasive nature and high temporal resolution. Spectral analysis of EEG signals reveals two key components: oscillatory activity associated with cognitive processes such as attention, memory, and perception; and aperiodic activity that reflects scale-free neural processes.

pmc-12613769.title: Simulations using APSIM suggest that Conservation Agriculture sustains protein yield under changing climate dynamics in Northern Mozambique
pmc-12613769.creator: Baqir Lalani, David Parsons, Mukhtar Ahmed, Uttam Kumar
pmc-12613769.description: BackgroundConservation Agriculture (CA) is based on the simultaneous practice of three principles: (i) no or minimum mechanical soil disturbance, (ii) permanent soil cover, and (iii) crop diversity e.g. crop rotation and/or intercropping systems. In parts of Sub Saharan Africa (SSA), conventional tillage practice is still pervasive and includes the practice of crop burning, resulting in severe soil erosion.

pmc-13030721.title: Trace-LogVector-Based Relational Retrieval for Conversational System Log Analysis
pmc-13030721.creator: Sun-Chul Park, Young-Han Kim
pmc-13030721.description: Highlights What are the main findings? A relational log representation, Trace-LogVector (TLV), consistently improves retrieval accuracy in RAG-based system log analysis compared to single-chunk representations.CARD-based multi-chunk construction preserves execution contexts and entity relationships, leading to substantial gains in Hit@5 and MRR@5 metrics. What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-13247589.title: Growth hormone retesting for idiopathic isolated growth hormone deficiency during and after puberty: a systematic review
pmc-13247589.creator: Joeri Vliegenthart, Deveney F Wols, Jan M Wit, Wichor Bramer, Edmond H H M Rings, Erica L T van den Akker, Danielle C M van der Kaay
pmc-13247589.description: ContextIdiopathic isolated growth hormone deficiency (IIGHD) is difficult to diagnose due to the day-to-day variation in growth hormone (GH) secretion and limitations of GH stimulation testing (GHST). Although recombinant human GH (rhGH) is typically continued until near adult height (NAH), many patients no longer show deficiency at that point. The optimal timing and method for retesting GH secretion remain unclear.

pmc-13261813.title: Physicochemical behaviour of acetaminophen-Dimethyl Sulphoxide mixtures studied via dielectric spectroscopy
pmc-13261813.creator: Vinita Khatri, Prasanjit K. Dey
pmc-13261813.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). pmc-13341593.title: Variants in UGT1A1 and SLCO1B1 increase the risk of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia: a case-control study in subtropical China
pmc-13341593.creator: Wen-Fang Wang, Li-Sen Shi, Zeng-Wen Xing, Yan-Mei Han, Wei-Qiang Liu

pmc-13641965.title: Deep learning for automated detection and classification of temporomandibular joint disorders: A scoping review
pmc-13641965.creator: Husnul Hatimah, Irfan Sugianto, Barunawaty Yunus, Muhammad Fadil Hidayat, Rifaat Nurrahma
pmc-13641965.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeTo map the available evidence on the application of deep learning (DL) in the imaging-based detection and classification of temporomandibular joint disorders (TMDs), and to identify research trends, imaging modalities investigated, and gaps in the current literature.Materials and MethodsA comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Wiley Online Library, ScienceDirect, and Cochrane, covering publications between January 2015 and January 2025, without restrictions on language.
